HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD ?Court No. - 82 Case :- CRIMINAL MISC. BAIL APPLICATION No. - 41313 of 2022 Applicant :- Dheeraj Prasad Opposite Party :- State Of U.P.And 3 Others Counsel for Applicant :- Manvendra Nath Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Ankit Mishra,Shri Ram Pandey Hon'ble Ajai Kumar Srivastava-I,J.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard Sri Manvendra Nath Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Vinod Kumar Rai, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the entire record.

No one has appeared on behalf of opposite party No.2 to press this application despite the fact that the names of Sri Ankit Mishra, Advocate and Sri Shri Ram Pandey, Advocate have been shown in the cause list.

The instant application for bail has been moved on behalf of the applicant, Dheeraj Prasad with the prayer to enlarge him on bail in F.I.R./ Case Crime No.185 of 2022, under Sections 354, 376, 452,
506 I.P.C. and Sections 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Jahanaganj, District Azamgarh, during pendency of the trial.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the first information report is based on false and fabricated facts.

The accused/ applicant is innocent who has been falsely implicated in this case due to his prior acquaintance with the victim and also because of the fact that the family members of the victim did not relish their relationship.

sentences.text: His further submission is that according to High School certificate of the victim, her date of birth is recorded as 11.08.2004 and computed accordingly, her age on the alleged date of incident comes to be 17 years 10 months approximately, who is of mature understanding.
His next submission is that initially there is no allegation of rape upon the victim by the present accused/ applicant in the first information report.
The victim has stated that she was molested by the present accused/ applicant only.
In her statement recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C., the victim maintained the same stand and again she did not say anything about any alleged sexual assault except the incident of molestation.
His further submission is that as the prosecution case was based on false facts and nothing, as stated in the first information report, had happened on the alleged date of incident.
Therefore, initially, the victim refused to get herself medically examined.

However, after she stated, in an afterthought manner and after due consultation, in her statement recorded under Sections 164 Cr.P.C. that rape upon her committed by the present applicant, she went for medical examination.
However, report of medical examination of the victim reveals that no spermatozoa was found.

His next submission is that the afterthought averment of alleged rape in the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. is made with a view to falsely implicate the present accused/
applicant.

Learned counsel for the applicant has also submitted that the accused/ applicant is languishing in jail since 14.05.2022 who has no previous criminal history as stated in para-17 to the instant application for bail.

His further submission is that in case, the applicant is enlarged on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and he will also fully cooperate with the trial court in getting the trial concluded expeditiously.
He has also submitted that the applicant will not intimidate or pressurize the witnesses or any other persons acquainted with the facts of the present case.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of bail by submitting that though, the date of birth of the victim, according to High School certificate, is recorded as 11.08.2004.

However, the victim being a child is below 18 years of age and the applicant is said to have committed rape upon her, therefore, having regard to the seriousness of offence, the accused/ applicant does not deserve to be enlarged on bail.

However, the learned A.G.A. has been unable to dispute the other factual submissions advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant including the fact that in the first information report and in the statement of the victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., there was no averment regarding alleged commission of rape upon the victim by the present accused/ applicant.

Having heard the learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and upon perusal of record, it transpires that initially a first information report came to be lodged against the present applicant for the offence under Sections 354, 452, 506 I.P.C. only because in the first information report, there was no averment regarding rape against the present applicant.

sentences.text: The age of the victim, according to High School Certificate, is recorded as 11.08.2004 and computed accordingly, her age on the alleged date of incident is reported to be 17 years 10 months approximately.
Initially, she refused to get herself medically examined.
However, after she stated in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. for the first time that allegedly, she was raped by the accused/ applicant, her medical examination was conducted.
However, medical examination report of the victim does not reveal any presence of spermatozoa.
The accused/ applicant is languishing in jail since 14.05.2022 who has no criminal history.

Thus, having regard to overall facts and circumstances of this case and also keeping in view the arguments advanced on behalf of the parties, the nature of offence, evidence regarding the complicity of applicant and without expressing any opinion on the merit of the case, a case for bail is made out.
The bail application is, thus, allowed.

If in the opinion of the trial court, default of this condition is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of his bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

sentences.text: The learned trial court is directed to proceed with the trial of the aforesaid case and conclude the same with utmost expedition keeping in view the provisions contained Section 35(2) POCSO Act, in accordance with law, without granting any unnecessary adjournments to the parties, if there is no other legal impediment.

S.S.P./S.P. and Joint Director Prosecution of the district concerned are directed to ensure that witnesses are present on the date fixed so that their testimonies may be recorded without there being any hindrance.

opennyai_summary.decision:
The bail application is, thus, allowed.
Let the applicant, Dheeraj Prasad be released on bail in the aforesaid case on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
1. The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/
pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial;
2. The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment;
3. The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail;
4.
If in the opinion of the trial court, default of this condition is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of his bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
The learned trial court is directed to proceed with the trial of the aforesaid case and conclude the same with utmost expedition keeping in view the provisions contained Section 35(2) POCSO Act, in accordance with law, without granting any unnecessary adjournments to the parties, if there is no other legal impediment.
S.S.P./S.P. and Joint Director Prosecution of the district concerned are directed to ensure that witnesses are present on the date fixed so that their testimonies may be recorded without there being any hindrance.
Office is directed to communicate this order to the S.S.P/S.P. and Joint Director Prosecution of the district concerned as well as trial court concerned separately for necessary compliance.
It is made clear that the trial of the aforesaid case shall be conducted without being influenced by any observation made herein above which are confined to the disposal of the instant application for bail.
